callout.title: Protect the reviewer bottleneck before buying more volume
callout.body: Enterprise origination usually fails at qualification, evidence, or handoff before it fails at raw contact supply.
items: Attach the original dated trigger to every account brief; a refreshed intent dashboard must not overwrite the evidence supporting an earlier fee.
Price research rework by defect category, separating missing evidence from client-requested changes after the brief was accepted.
Maintain a second trained reviewer for the ten accounts closest to fee acceptance; a single absent employee should not stop billing.
Track owner rescue hours by mapped play, then rewrite the three most rescue-intensive handoffs before adding contractor production capacity.

sections.heading: 2. Run one weekly scorecard from source evidence to accepted fees
paragraphs: Run a forty-five-minute weekly operating review from a frozen CRM extract, not from contractor slide decks. Give every measure an owner, denominator, cohort date, source field, and corrective action. Account-brief acceptance equals accepted briefs divided by reviewed briefs; meeting attendance equals attended meetings divided by meetings scheduled to occur during the period. Qualified-opportunity acceptance equals client-accepted opportunities divided by submitted opportunities whose contractual review period has expired. Report pending submissions separately so delayed buyer responses do not artificially improve the ratio. Measure acceptance turnaround, first-pass defects, duplicate accounts, disputed fees, and aged receivables alongside production. Establish initial internal targets of at least ninety-five percent first-pass brief acceptance and ninety percent on-time evidence review, then recalibrate using actual cohort performance. These are operating targets rather than market benchmarks. Separate activity metrics from commercial outcomes: email opens are unreliable instrumentation, meeting bookings can conceal no-shows, and pipeline value belongs to the client. A million-dollar prospect contract remains a prospect contract even when the pod originated the introduction. The operator earns only the retainer and opportunity fees supported by its own agreement.

Resolve attribution before launch by defining eligible accounts, excluded existing opportunities, attribution windows, duplicate treatment, required buyer roles, and the client's acceptance authority. In Salesforce, preserve campaign membership, original source, opportunity creation time, submission time, and acceptance time as distinct facts. A correction should create an auditable history rather than silently replace the original field. Store the supporting email or portal decision with controlled access and a record identifier. Calendly attendance data can corroborate a meeting, but scheduling alone cannot prove enterprise qualification. Require a human reviewer to verify fit, need, buyer involvement, and the agreed next step before submission. Inspect all billable opportunities and a risk-weighted sample of nonbillable research outputs. If acceptance drops, split failures into wrong account, weak buyer role, missing evidence, duplicate opportunity, or client definition change. Assign corrections to the responsible workflow rather than increasing outbound volume. Compensate contractors for accepted deliverables within their control; a modest quality bonus can reward sustained low defects without paying for inflated pipeline estimates. Preserve a separate dispute register with amount, reason, responsible reviewer, and resolution deadline.

Treat outreach permissions and suppression as measurable delivery requirements, not a separate appendix that production ignores. For commercial email, 15 U.S.C. section 7704 governs matters including truthful transmission information, required identification, postal address, and opt-out handling. Process opt-outs internally within one business day, comfortably inside the federal ten-business-day deadline, and propagate them across sequencers and subcontractor lists. Calls and texts require channel-specific review under 47 CFR section 64.1200, including applicable consent and do-not-call requirements; a business contact label does not automatically resolve a mobile-number restriction. Where the California Consumer Privacy Act applies, map collection notices, purposes, retention, and service-provider terms to the actual processing relationship. Keep a permitted-use record for every data source and prohibit contractors from exporting client lists into personal prospecting accounts. The weekly review should surface suppression failures, unauthorized exports, and incomplete permission evidence as immediate stop-work conditions for affected records. Pause the relevant channel or cohort while preserving unaffected delivery. Sector-specific referral rules also matter: do not transplant a technology prospecting fee schedule into healthcare, securities, or federal contracting without evaluating the applicable compensation restrictions.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile canonical profits to accrual cohorts and concentration limits
paragraphs: Keep the three canonical cases intact: Conservative revenue is $150,000 with $30,000 owner net profit at twenty percent; Base revenue is $675,000 with $202,500 profit at thirty percent; Scaled revenue is $1,200,000 with $480,000 profit at forty percent. Their implied total annual costs are $120,000, $472,500, and $720,000 respectively. Monthly revenue averages are $12,500, $56,250, and $100,000; monthly profit averages are $2,500, $16,875, and $40,000. Retainers plus earned qualified-opportunity fees must reconcile to those revenue totals without adding client contract values. The stated $4,000–$20,000 monthly opex range cannot be treated as the complete expense ceiling for every scenario: Base and Scaled imply average total monthly costs of $39,375 and $60,000. Build a cost bridge separating payroll, contractor purchases, data, software, selling expense, and overhead. The Conservative five-person configuration presents a genuine labor-budget constraint. Its $120,000 total cost envelope does not demonstrate that two market-rate full-time employees and three contractors are funded. Preserve the scorecard while requiring an explicit compensation and utilization plan; do not hide unpaid owner labor or outside subsidies inside apparent operating efficiency.

Close the books monthly using an accrual policy aligned with the actual promises in each contract. A retainer collected before delivery is initially deferred to the extent services remain unperformed; recognize it as the contracted service obligation is satisfied rather than assuming every retainer is automatically earned on receipt. Record opportunity fees when the agreed earning conditions and applicable revenue-recognition requirements are met. Assess variable consideration and reversals where acceptance or clawback terms create uncertainty. Accrue contractor costs for accepted work even when the invoice arrives later. Use QuickBooks Online or Xero tracking dimensions for client, service month, and acquisition cohort, with the CRM opportunity identifier retained as supporting detail. Reconcile beginning receivables plus invoices less cash and credits to ending receivables, separately reconciling earned unbilled revenue and deferred balances. Report client contribution after attributable delivery costs, then show shared labor and overhead below that line. Never label contribution as owner net profit. Review cohort retention using starting recurring fees, expansion, contraction, and churn, excluding new clients from existing-client retention calculations. Long enterprise sales cycles make signed backlog, recognized revenue, invoiced amounts, and collected cash four different operational facts.

Set a maximum twenty-five percent exposure to any customer group and any ultimate paying counterparty, measured separately on trailing-twelve-month earned fees, current receivables, and forward contracted fees. Aggregate affiliates under common control and identify the principal behind agencies or channel partners. Four equal clients technically meet the ceiling but leave no tolerance for one cancellation or uneven fee timing; six to eight balanced relationships provide more practical headroom. A new business with one or two clients will breach the policy, so label that condition explicitly, maintain a dated diversification plan, and do not describe the book as diversified or exit-ready. Freeze discretionary expansion of an over-limit relationship while pursuing other accounts; perform existing obligations rather than manufacturing diversification by relabeling invoices. Apply the same twenty-five percent ceiling to intermediary-controlled fee receipts so multiple end clients cannot disguise dependence on one reseller. Track origination-channel dependence separately and build replacement paths for critical vendors. Stress-test the loss of the largest customer using avoidable costs, notice periods, receivable timing, and retained payroll. Maintain a liquidity plan that covers the actual stressed cash deficit; a profitable accrual statement alone cannot fund a delayed enterprise payment.

sections.heading: 4. Sell transferable earnings or retain a resilient cash business
paragraphs: Build valuation from verified maintainable earnings, not from client pipeline or a headline revenue multiple. Small owner-operated service firms may be discussed on seller's discretionary earnings, while businesses with independent management may be evaluated on adjusted EBITDA. Use two to three times verified SDE and three to five times transferable EBITDA as illustrative negotiating ranges, not observed transaction comparables for this candidate. Actual pricing depends on size, recurrence, growth quality, concentration, and deal structure. Canonical owner net profit is neither automatically SDE nor automatically EBITDA. Prepare a bridge covering owner compensation already expensed, replacement management, interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, and supportable nonrecurring items. If diligence establishes Base SDE of exactly $202,500, the illustrative two-to-three-times range produces $405,000–$607,500 of enterprise value. That conditional example does not prove the bridge. For Scaled, if the $480,000 owner profit needs $150,000 of incremental replacement management and all other EBITDA adjustments net to zero, transferable EBITDA is $330,000; three to five times yields $990,000–$1,650,000. Subtract debt, account for agreed cash and working-capital adjustments, and distinguish cash at closing from contingent consideration before estimating seller proceeds.

Make the data room an operating byproduct rather than a last-minute reconstruction. Maintain signed client contracts, amendments, renewal dates, termination rights, assignment provisions, acceptance logs, monthly cohort statements, and the complete thirty-play ownership register. Retain signed contractor copyright assignments satisfying 17 U.S.C. section 204(a) where a transfer is intended; payment alone does not transfer copyright, and commissioned work does not automatically qualify as work made for hire. Identify preexisting templates, licensed datasets, software subscriptions, and third-party assets separately so the seller cannot promise rights they do not own. Check whether data and vendor licenses survive a transaction and whether client assignment requires consent. Use company-controlled password management, named accounts, least-privilege access, and a documented offboarding checklist. Share diligence records through staged, access-controlled folders, redacting personal information until disclosure is necessary and permitted. Demonstrate transferability with backup-led client meetings, repeatable acceptance decisions, and a tested recovery procedure for CRM automations. A buyer should be able to trace a sampled fee from agreement to source evidence, acceptance, ledger, and cash without interviewing the founder to reconstruct what happened.

Negotiate quality of proceeds as carefully as the headline multiple. A large earnout tied to the buyer's future sales execution can transfer enterprise sales-cycle risk back to the seller. Define any contingent payment using auditable retained fees or specified accepted opportunities, with clear accounting policies, information rights, allocation rules, and dispute procedures. Prevent related-party charges or reassigned accounts from silently changing the measurement base. Model seller transition hours and any post-close employment separately from purchase price. For an owner who retains the business, the same discipline supports cash distributions: fund tax obligations, working capital, replacement labor, and downside liquidity before distributing the remaining cash. Compare a risk-adjusted hold case against net closing proceeds plus realistically collectible deferred consideration, rather than comparing annual profit with an unadjusted headline offer. Review the comparison quarterly without forcing a sale timetable. The thirty mapped plays become valuable intellectual property only when another authorized operator can execute them using documented inputs, budgets, acceptance standards, and exception rules. Premium outcomes come from reduced dependence and clean evidence; adding more contractors, campaigns, or theoretical pipeline does not substitute for transferable customer relationships and durable earned fees.

chapters.question_prompt: What is the exact Day-1-to-Day-30 execution schedule for launching million-dollar lead generation, and what quantitative thresholds govern Kill, Fix, or Scale decisions at Day 30/60/90?
chapters.title: The First 30-Day Launch Sprint & Kill / Fix / Scale Gates
chapters.subtitle: A Five-Person ABM Sprint With Salesforce Evidence, CAN-SPAM Controls, Accepted-Opportunity Economics, and Day-30/60/90 Decisions
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #21, Million-Dollar Lead Generation, ranks #18 with an 86/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter turns its 30 mapped plays into a daily execution sequence for a two-employee, three-contractor pod: define one enterprise buying problem, instrument attribution, test a bounded account cohort, and sell evidence-backed opportunity creation. The first 30 days establish operating proof; the stated three-to-twelve-month time to first deal prevents confusing early meetings with enterprise contract wins. Annual owner profit remains $30,000 Conservative, $202,500 Base, and $480,000 Scaled. A $15,000 first-month spending ceiling, explicit cohort denominators, and Day-30/60/90 Kill, Fix, or Scale thresholds keep client contract values outside operator revenue and keep expansion subordinate to cash, attribution, and delivery capacity.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Bound the Offer, Budget, Evidence, and Five-Person Pod
paragraphs: Start Day 1 with one client profile, one buying problem, and one geographic market. Candidate #21 targets enterprise contract demand generation, not the resale of scraped contact lists. Its 30 mapped operator plays become thirty daily work packages here, labeled P01 through P30 as chapter-local implementation labels rather than a claim about an external play catalog. The founder, employee one, owns offer design, client discovery, commercial terms, and opportunity acceptance. Employee two owns Salesforce or HubSpot architecture, suppression, scheduling, and reporting. Contractor one researches accounts; contractor two writes and tests messages; contractor three conducts independent quality checks and supports specialist reviews. Those are five people, not five unlimited delivery lanes. Reserve forty hours weekly for each employee and cap each contractor at ten hours initially. Allocate employee time before adding accounts: twenty hours for client work, twenty for research review, twenty for outreach operations, ten for measurement, and ten for corrections. Record contractor assignments separately. Choose an enterprise problem with observable triggers, such as an announced infrastructure migration, procurement event, or executive mandate. A large company alone is not an actionable signal. Require a dated source and a plausible buying committee before admitting an account.

Set a first-month cash ceiling of $15,000 before purchasing data. The illustrative allocation is $8,000 for loaded employee compensation, $3,000 for contractors, $1,500 for software, $750 for research access, and $1,750 for specialist review and contingency. These are spending limits, not claims that every labor market supports this staffing cost. If actual loaded compensation exceeds its allowance, reduce scope or secure additional explicitly budgeted capital before committing the pod; do not erase employee costs by labeling founder labor free. This launch sits within the canonical $15,000–$100,000 startup capital range and $4,000–$20,000 monthly operating range. The chosen ninety-day test requires $45,000 of available launch cash if receipts remain zero. An operator starting with only $15,000 can fund this first month, not promise the full test. Track cash paid, irrevocable commitments, and refundable deposits separately every Friday. Stop new discretionary commitments at $12,000 during month one, preserving the remaining $3,000 inside the ceiling for payroll, corrections, and exit work. Cancel unused enrichment seats before renewal. Never purchase an annual intent-data subscription merely to obtain a short trial, and never count an unsigned retainer proposal as available cash.

By Day 7, the acceptance specification must distinguish a positive reply, a held discovery meeting, and a client-accepted opportunity. A positive reply expresses relevant business interest; an unsubscribe or automated response does not qualify. A held meeting requires attendance by the prospect and documented discussion of the target problem. An accepted opportunity additionally requires a named account, a suitable stakeholder or documented route to authority, a confirmed problem, a plausible funding path, a dated next action, and the client's recorded acceptance. Do not manufacture a committed budget when the prospect only describes an investigation. The client receives five business days to accept or dispute each evidence packet; silence does not trigger an opportunity fee. Put duplicate-account lookback, existing-pipeline exclusions, attribution precedence, refunds, and dispute handling into the signed scope. For commercial email, implement 15 U.S.C. § 7704 controls covering accurate routing information, nondeceptive subjects, required identification, postal address, and an effective opt-out. Apply the applicable jurisdiction and sector rules before activating a channel. Federal procurement contingent fees require specific review under FAR Subpart 3.4; healthcare referrals can implicate 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b). Keep those segments outside the initial offer until its compensation structure has been reviewed.

callout.title: Four Verifications Before the First Real Send
callout.body: The founder records evidence for each check; a failed check blocks the affected activity rather than disappearing into a meeting note.
items: Verify that actual payroll, contractor commitments, and subscriptions fit the $15,000 first-month ceiling with no dependence on unsigned proposals.
Verify source provenance and suppression behavior using five synthetic records, including an opted-out contact and an existing client opportunity.
Verify that the client has explicitly agreed to the six-field acceptance packet, duplicate lookback, dispute process, and opportunity-fee trigger.
Verify channel and sector applicability before using telephone automation, covered personal data, healthcare referrals, or federal procurement compensation.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Instrument Attribution and Release a Bounded Account Cohort
paragraphs: Use Days 8 through 10 to make the evidence trail stronger than the pitch. Salesforce campaign membership or HubSpot campaign properties should preserve account identifier, contact identifier, source URL, observation date, outreach version, delivery result, reply classification, meeting status, and client disposition. Store immutable event timestamps in UTC and retain the original source excerpt where permitted. Account attribution must precede contact-level enthusiasm: three responding employees at one company are one responding account, not three opportunities. Build a client-supplied exclusion list covering customers, active deals, partner-owned accounts, and previously rejected domains. Reconcile that list before each batch rather than relying on a single kickoff export. Use Calendly routing or the CRM scheduler only after the prospect expresses interest; a calendar booking without attendance is not a held meeting. Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for the sending domain, inspect reply routing, and test unsubscribe processing. Authentication supports reliable delivery but does not authorize outreach. Do not rotate domains to escape provider restrictions. Keep a documented retention schedule and minimize exported contact fields. Where the California Consumer Privacy Act applies, Civil Code § 1798.100 requires attention to collection notices, purpose limits, and retention; a business email address does not automatically remove a person from the statute's scope.

Release the first twenty accounts on Day 11, inspect results on Day 12, and release the remainder on Day 14 only after correcting defects. The initial cohort contains 100 distinct accounts and at least 150 distinct delivered contacts, with no more than two selected stakeholders per account. Delivery means the receiving system accepted the message; it does not establish inbox placement or human attention. Count distinct contacted people, not every follow-up message, in the contact denominator. A mature account has received its first valid message at least fourteen calendar days before the decision snapshot. This makes the Day-14 cohort eligible for the Day-30 review while leaving room for delayed ingestion. If delivery defects prevent 100 accounts from maturing, classify the review as Fix for insufficient exposure, not Kill for market failure. Limit each contact to three relevant touches over fourteen days, ending immediately on refusal or opt-out. Use one problem-led message and one controlled alternative; changing the audience, offer, and copy together destroys diagnostic value. Pause a batch above 2% hard bounces or on any complaint pending inspection. Those are internal safety thresholds, not universal provider limits. Record attempted delivery separately so bounce rates retain the correct denominator.

Automate clerical work, not unsupported assertions about buying intent. Apollo or ZoomInfo may supply licensed contact attributes, while first-party account research establishes whether the account actually fits the offer. LinkedIn Sales Navigator can support manual role verification within its permitted use. An announced acquisition can justify a research hypothesis; it does not prove allocated budget for the client's service. Require the researcher to distinguish observed facts from inferred needs inside separate CRM fields. The operations employee reviews every record in the first twenty-account batch, then checks a random twenty records from each subsequent hundred-account cohort. Any missing provenance, prohibited source, or suppression error freezes the affected batch until corrected. Message production should use a reusable problem statement, account-specific evidence, and a low-friction request for relevance confirmation. Avoid fabricated personal familiarity and claims of relationships that do not exist. The copy contractor drafts; the founder owns factual accuracy; the quality contractor tests the final rendered version. Keep enrichment and scheduling permissions separate from billing permissions. A webhook can propose a meeting-status update, but it cannot create a billable opportunity without documented client acceptance. This division preserves automation leverage while preventing a convenient integration from silently rewriting the commercial contract.

callout.title: Protect Signal Quality Before Buying More Reach
callout.body: Enterprise demand generation fails quietly when contact activity substitutes for account evidence.
items: Ask the client for active-opportunity exclusions before showing campaign results; retrospective exclusions invite disputes over successful accounts.
Preserve the exact trigger excerpt and observation date so a later stakeholder change does not erase the rationale for outreach.
Separate rescheduled meetings from new meetings in CRM reporting; one prospect moving a calendar slot must never increase production counts.
Use the first twenty-account batch to expose data defects, not to declare a winning conversion rate from a tiny sample.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Convert Replies Into Accepted Evidence and Test Unit Economics
paragraphs: During week three, the founder spends protected time on discovery instead of repeatedly rewriting outbound copy. Respond to relevant positive replies within one business day and offer two meeting windows matched to the prospect's time zone. Confirm the business problem before involving the client's senior seller. A reply requesting a brochure may justify nurturing but does not establish a qualified opportunity. The discovery record should capture the prospect's words, decision process, current approach, constraints, funding path, and agreed next action. Record calls only when applicable recording requirements have been satisfied; otherwise use contemporaneous notes and a written recap. Send the client an acceptance packet within one business day of a held meeting. Keep client review latency visible because a slow client can make a productive campaign appear unproductive. Pending packets remain outside accepted totals. Disputed packets enter a separate queue with a named reason and evidence request. The quality contractor checks all early packets for unsupported budget claims, duplicate accounts, invented authority, and missing next steps. The operations employee reconciles calendar attendance against CRM status each afternoon. These mundane controls protect both fee collectability and the client's sales capacity; sending weak meetings to an enterprise seller consumes scarce credibility faster than it creates pipeline.

For this sprint, use an illustrative offer of a $7,500 monthly retainer plus $2,500 for each client-accepted opportunity. This is a test price, not an alternative scorecard or an instruction to charge an impermissible sector-specific contingent fee. Three accepted opportunities produce $15,000 of earned monthly operator fees if the retainer service and acceptance conditions are satisfied: $7,500 plus three times $2,500. Cash arrives only when paid. At the full $15,000 monthly cost ceiling, that month produces zero operating surplus before any additional unbudgeted cost; early traction does not establish the canonical 30% Base margin. Track recognized revenue, invoices, collections, and credits in separate ledger columns. The canonical annual cases remain $150,000 revenue less $120,000 costs for $30,000 owner profit; $675,000 less $472,500 for $202,500; and $1,200,000 less $720,000 for $480,000. Those all-in annual cost amounts must not be replaced by twelve times the launch software budget. The quoted monthly operating range describes a launch planning envelope, not the complete scaled expense model. Client contracts worth millions belong in the client's pipeline, never in operator revenue. Preserve the canonical two-employee, three-contractor staffing for Conservative and Base, and three employees plus four contractors for Scaled.

Measure launch efficiency with two different cost views. Fully loaded launch cost per accepted opportunity equals cumulative launch expense divided by cumulative accepted opportunities. At $15,000 and three accepted opportunities, that figure is $5,000. Marginal fulfillment cost measures the additional research, coordination, and review needed for the next opportunity; cap that modeled amount at $1,250 against a $2,500 opportunity fee before expanding. Do not allocate the same retainer twice when calculating contribution. Separately track account yield, held-meeting attendance, client rejection reasons, and hours consumed per packet. The founder needs evidence that the pod can service incremental work without abandoning existing clients. Maintain at least twenty percent unused scheduled capacity across the delivery tasks most likely to bottleneck. If the founder is the only person able to qualify meetings, spare research hours do not solve the constraint. By Day 21, compare actual time records against the original weekly allocation and remove low-value custom reporting before buying more accounts. Expect early ratios to remain noisy: the model describes internal decision thresholds, not industry averages. Require prospect evidence and client acceptance together; neither a persuasive sales narrative nor an attractive spreadsheet can replace the other when deciding whether to continue spending.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Reviews at 60/90: Apply Explicit Kill, Fix, or Scale Rules
paragraphs: Week four closes the measurement loop rather than staging a premature victory announcement. Freeze the Day-30 snapshot at a declared UTC time and export the account cohort, event history, opportunity packets, spending ledger, and capacity log. Use cumulative mature cohorts of 100 accounts at Day 30, 200 at Day 60, and 300 at Day 90, with at least 150, 300, and 450 distinct delivered contacts respectively. Complete each additional hundred-account release by Day 44 and Day 74 so its exposure can mature before review. If the preceding decision stops outreach, do not force those later cohort targets by bypassing the stop. Count each account once in positive-response and accepted-opportunity totals, and count each distinct attended discovery meeting once in meeting totals. The expansion targets are eight, sixteen, and twenty-four positive accounts; four, eight, and twelve held meetings; and three, six, and nine accepted opportunities at the respective reviews. These are chosen operating hurdles, not predictions. A client deal closing after ninety days is compatible with the canonical three-to-twelve-month first-deal window. Early commercial proof means someone pays for the operator's defined service; it does not mean the client's enterprise buyer has already signed a million-dollar agreement.

Apply decisions in a fixed order. First stop affected activity for unlawful sourcing, broken suppression, materially false claims, or unreliable attribution, and resolve the defect before any restart. Next test cash: cumulative launch spending cannot exceed $15,000, $30,000, and $45,000 at the three reviews. New discretionary commitments stop when cash available after existing obligations cannot cover the next thirty days of the approved operating plan. Then evaluate market evidence. At Day 30, Kill the current segment-offer combination if a mature, technically sound cohort produces zero held meetings and fewer than three positive accounts. At Day 60, Kill it if 200 mature accounts produce zero accepted opportunities after one documented correction cycle. At Day 90, Kill it if 300 mature accounts produce fewer than three accepted opportunities after two correction cycles, or if no paying operator-service client exists. Kill means stop this hypothesis and its discretionary spending, not declare the entire market impossible. Fix covers all noncritical outcomes between Kill and Scale, including insufficient exposure. Run one fourteen-day correction against one diagnosed bottleneck. Review the correction on its scheduled date without postponing the original Day-60 or Day-90 cash and evidence checkpoints.

Scale requires every review-specific production target plus clean attribution, no unresolved invoice disputes, marginal fulfillment cost at or below $1,250, and twenty percent spare bottleneck capacity. It also requires a paying operator-service client, collected cash covering at least fifty percent of cumulative launch spending, and cash available after obligations sufficient for the next thirty days. At Day 90, additionally require the latest thirty days of earned operator revenue to cover that period's fully loaded operating costs; deposits for future work cannot satisfy this test. Increase the next batch by no more than twenty-five percent and recalculate staffing before adding another client. This bounded increase is not authorization to jump directly to the canonical Scaled team. When only one paying client exists, treat concentration as an explicit experiment risk and make no client-dependent permanent hire. Once three clients are active, require the largest to contribute no more than fifty percent of trailing ninety-day earned revenue before adding fixed capacity. Reconcile every proposed expansion with the annual scorecard rather than annualizing one unusually strong month. The Day-30 deliverable is a signed decision record stating denominator, results, cash, owner, next action, and review date. That record makes stopping a disciplined operating choice instead of an argument about optimism.
